messages:
jen (sdk): Hey folks — running into a couple of flaky issues in the .NET SDK: socket exhaustion in long‑running services (we create a new HttpClient per request in a few places), and another one where streaming responses sometimes never finish when combined with our Polly retry policy. Anyone seen these patterns and have recommendations?
kevin (eng-net): 100% seen both. For socket exhaustion: stop new HttpClient per request. Use IHttpClientFactory or a singleton HttpClient. Also look at SocketsHttpHandler settings (PooledConnectionLifetime) to avoid stale DNS.
maria (eng): For the streaming + Polly problem: if you retry after the response body has started, you can leak streams or reuse a connection that’s mid‑stream. Best practice is to either buffer the body before retrying or make the policy not retry when ResponseContent is started.
jen (sdk): Ah great point. We're using AddPolicyHandler on the client. Any pattern for skipping retries once reading starts?
kevin (eng-net): One pattern: use HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead when you want to stream, then the moment you start reading the response stream you should prevent retries. In Polly you can use an ExecutionContext flag. Example: when sending request, pass context with "streaming": true, then in the retry policy check ctx.TryGet("streaming", out var s) and skip retry if true.
maria (eng): Also consider this code snippet:

```csharp
var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, url);
var response = await client.SendAsync(request, HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead, ct);
response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();
using var stream = await response.Content.ReadAsStreamAsync(ct);
// stream -> copy to destination (don't buffer entire content)
await stream.CopyToAsync(destinationStream, 81920, ct);
```

If you need retries, do them before you start copying.
jen (sdk): Good. What about IHttpClientFactory setup for PooledConnectionLifetime example?
kevin (eng-net): Example:

```csharp
services.AddHttpClient("redwood")
  .ConfigurePrimaryHttpMessageHandler(() => new SocketsHttpHandler
  {
    PooledConnectionLifetime = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5),
    MaxConnectionsPerServer = 50
  });
```

That avoids long-lived sockets holding old DNS. Also don't forget DefaultRequestVersion / VersionPolicy if you care about HTTP/2 multiplexing.
maria (eng): Another subtlety: if you use Polly retry that disposes and reuses the same HttpRequestMessage instance, it can fail since HttpRequestMessage content streams are not rewindable. Use a factory to recreate the request on each retry, or set HttpRequestMessage.Content = new StringContent(body) each time.
jen (sdk): Oof — we were reusing the same HttpRequestMessage for POSTs in our integration test harness. That would explain the weird 400s after a retry.
kevin (eng-net): For non-idempotent methods, be conservative with retries. For streaming uploads/downloads, consider chunked uploads or resumable logic at app layer instead of automatic retries.
maria (eng): Quick tip for diagnostics: enable SocketsHttpHandler logging and set ServicePointManager.DnsRefreshTimeout when using older handlers. Also check RuntimeSockets stats if you're on Linux.
jen (sdk): Thanks, that's actionable. I'll refactor to use AddHttpClient + configure handler, change our retry policy to avoid retrying once streaming starts, and fix the request recreation. Will open a PR. :thumbsup:
